note: The OLG covers the core SE income budgeting scenarios well: (1) 12-month annualization for annual income earned in a shorter period (Self-Employment SNAP > Averaging Self-Employment Income), (2) elective averaging for fluctuating earned income over the certification period (Types of Earned Income > Income Averaging), and (3) proration for partial-year SE income (Self-Employment SNAP > Example, covering summer vendors and new businesses). The OLG also has an 'Anticipating Self-Employment Income' section for non-averaged SE income. However, the OLG does not explicitly state the FNS rule that steady SE income 'that can be reasonably anticipated month to month' does not need to be annualized, averaged, or prorated — the existence of the anticipation section implies this pathway but never articulates the condition clearly. Additionally, the OLG's fluctuating income averaging guidance is in the general earned income section (Types of Earned Income > Income Averaging), not in the Self-Employment SNAP page itself, which could cause workers to miss that SE income can be electively averaged when it fluctuates. The FNS provisions regarding unreported SE income sources and QC reviewer correction procedures are QC-specific and not applicable to the OLG's caseworker audience.
